record.evidence_text: Without the continuous load of Earth’s gravity, the living tissues of bone reshape themselves. Freed from pressures of Earth’s surface, cells that build new bone slow down their work. Cells that remove old bone keep chugging along. Removal outpaces growth, producing weaker, more brittle bones.
